name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,767

entries.clue: Drink around fourth-rate spot, one shouldn't go down here (8)

indicatorNotes.around: the drink goes around the other pieces, holding them inside

blocks.note: wine, a drink; it wraps round the rest
grades run A, B, C, D, so a fourth-rate mark is D
a pip is a spot on a die or domino

annotation.surface: A dingy bar at a seedy spot where you'd think twice before downing anything.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: food or drink going down the windpipe instead of the gullet is what makes you choke, so it is the place nothing should go down.
annotation.definitionFit: Swallowed food should never go down the windpipe, the airway to the lungs.

entries.clue: Animal appeal with one furry foot raised (6)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, lifting the letters makes them read bottom to top

blocks.note: 'it' is sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'
I is the Roman numeral one
an animal's furry foot

annotation.surface: A creature with charm, holding up one furry paw.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' looks like a plea; in crosswords it often means sex appeal. The furry foot sits so comfortably in the animal picture that it hides being a building block.
annotation.definitionFit: The wapiti is a large North American deer, also called the elk.

entries.clue: Killer skirts from Nagoya enthralling fashionable Japan (5)

indicatorNotes.skirts from: a word's skirts are its edges, so take its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.enthralling: to enthral is to hold captive, so the outer letters hold the rest

blocks.note: the outside letters of NagoyA
in = fashionable
J is the international vehicle code for Japan

annotation.surface: A dangerous woman in fashionable skirts from a Japanese city charming the whole nation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Skirts' looks like clothing in a fashion story; it means the edges of Nagoya. The Japanese setting fits the answer, a Japanese assassin.
annotation.definitionFit: A ninja was a trained Japanese covert agent and assassin.

entries.clue: Endure each part before finale of "Walküre" (9)

indicatorNotes.finale of: a finale is the ending, so the last letter

blocks.note: per = each, as in 'a pound per head'
to part is to sever, cut apart
the last letter of WalkürE

annotation.surface: Advice to sit through every act of a very long Wagner opera until the end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part' reads as a section of the opera, and it is a verb meaning cut. Die Walküre is one of the four long operas of Wagner's Ring cycle, so enduring it is apt.
annotation.definitionFit: To persevere is to keep going despite difficulty, to endure.

entries.clue: Secure, compared to American stars (7)

blocks.note: to peg something is to fix it in place
as, the word of comparison ('as tall as')
US = American

annotation.surface: Someone feeling safe next to Hollywood's big names.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stars' tempts you towards film celebrities alongside 'American'; here it means a constellation in the night sky.
annotation.definitionFit: Pegasus is a constellation, a group of stars named after the winged horse.
annotation.definitionNote: Plural 'stars' names a constellation, which is a single thing made of many stars.

entries.clue: Shaking butts, couple of fellows dance (3-3)

indicatorNotes.Shaking butts: to shake off something is to get rid of it; a butt is the end of a thing, so each word loses its last letter

blocks.note: a chap is a fellow; a couple of them is CHAP twice
each CHAP drops its end letter P

annotation.surface: Two men wiggling their bottoms on the dance floor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Butts' reads as bottoms, which suits a dance; in the wordplay the butts are the ends of each CHAP. 'Shaking' means shedding them, not wiggling them.
annotation.definitionFit: The cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance.

entries.clue: Swarms VIPs at the Oscars (5)

blocks.note: a host is a great crowd, as in 'a host of daffodils'
the presenters who front the Oscars ceremony

annotation.surface: Crowds of famous guests mobbing the Academy Awards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swarms' reads as a verb, with the VIPs doing the swarming; it is really a plural noun, a multitude.
annotation.definitionFit: Hosts are both large crowds and the presenters running the Oscars.

entries.clue: They return bags left during parties (9)

indicatorNotes.during: one thing happening during another sits inside it

blocks.note: carouses are drunken revels
L = left

annotation.surface: Guests who hand back handbags forgotten at parties.
annotation.walkthrough: L goes into CAROUSES just before the final S. The definition is the airport sort: a carousel is the rotating belt that brings luggage back to passengers.
annotation.definitionFit: Baggage carousels deliver passengers' bags back to them after a flight.

entries.clue: Craving a little quiet inside (8)

indicatorNotes.inside: the quiet letter goes inside the phrase

blocks.note: a + petite, meaning little
p = piano, quiet in music

annotation.surface: A mild longing, or a secret hunger kept to oneself.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A little quiet' reads as one phrase meaning 'rather muted'; split it as A + PETITE with P, quiet, inside after the A.
annotation.definitionFit: An appetite is a craving, for food or anything else.

entries.clue: Write something boring about ancient royal (9)

blocks.note: to pen is to write
a drag is a tedious thing
on = about, as in 'a talk on birds'

annotation.surface: An instruction to produce a dull essay about some old king.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like drilling or like a dull essay; it gives DRAG. Uther Pendragon, in Arthurian legend, was King Arthur's father.
annotation.definitionFit: Pendragon was a title of ancient British chief kings, borne by Uther, King Arthur's father.

entries.clue: Low sodium cleanse on the rise (5)

indicatorNotes.on the rise: in a down clue, rising letters read upwards

blocks.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
to rid a place of something is to cleanse it

annotation.surface: A low-salt detox diet that is catching on.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like health advice about a low-sodium cleanse, but 'Low' is the definition by itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Originally the point of the sky directly underfoot, the word now means the lowest ebb of anything, as in 'an all-time low'.
annotation.definitionNote: 'Low' here is a noun, a low point, as in 'an all-time low'.

entries.clue: Bit in fight (5)

blocks.note: a small leftover piece, as of paper or food
an informal word for a scuffle or brawl

annotation.surface: Someone got bitten during a brawl.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bit' reads as the past of bite; it is a noun, a small piece.
annotation.definitionFit: A scrap is both a small fragment and a brief fight.

entries.clue: Intro to tuneless composer's passages (7)

indicatorNotes.Intro to: an intro is the opening, so the first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of Tuneless
Ravel's, belonging to the French composer Maurice Ravel

annotation.surface: A critic sneering at the opening of some unmelodic composer's musical passages.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passages' sits in a musical sentence as bits of a score; it means journeys, as in a passage to India.
annotation.definitionFit: A passage can be a voyage, as in 'booking a passage'; the plural covers someone's journeys abroad.

entries.clue: Offend police inspectors with burst of wind (7)

blocks.note: DI = Detective Inspector, so DIs are police inspectors
a gust is a sudden rush of wind

annotation.surface: Someone breaking wind in front of the detectives.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is schoolboy humour about flatulence, which also happens to be disgusting.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to repel or sicken someone.

entries.clue: Certain Marxist's caught in deal with case of loot (8,5)

indicatorNotes.caught in: the first pieces are held inside the word for 'deal with'

blocks.note: sure = certain
Che's, belonging to Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary
to treat a matter is to deal with it

annotation.surface: A particular communist is arrested in a dodgy deal involving stolen goods.
annotation.walkthrough: The Marxist is Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary. 'Case of loot' looks like a criminal case in the surface; it is a box holding the loot.
annotation.definitionFit: A treasure chest is a box full of valuables.

entries.clue: National worry about keeping current subsides (9)

indicatorNotes.about: turned about, so the word reverses
indicatorNotes.keeping: the reversed word keeps the rest inside it

blocks.note: 'what's eating you?' means what's worrying you
I is the symbol for electric current
to wane is to diminish

annotation.surface: A country fretting over keeping its power supply as it dwindles.
annotation.walkthrough: EAT reversed is TAE, and it holds I + WANES between its TA and E. 'Current' looks like electricity in the surface, and it is: the physics symbol I.
annotation.definitionFit: A demonym used as a noun: a citizen of the island state off the Chinese coast.
annotation.definitionNote: 'National' is a noun, a citizen of a country.

entries.clue: Enamelwork loons, nice for breaking (9)

indicatorNotes.for breaking: the letters are due to be broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Delicate enamel ornaments, pleasant enough, about to be smashed by idiots.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface imagines fools and fragile ornaments; 'loons' is just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Cloisonné is enamel work in which colours are separated by thin metal strips.

entries.clue: Big wave concerning small cutters (8)

blocks.note: a surge is a great swell of water
on = concerning, about
S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A tidal wave hitting some little boats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cutters' look like small boats beside a big wave; they are people who cut for a living.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful description: operating on patients means cutting into them with a scalpel.

entries.clue: Fixed on Titian nude's powerful body (6,7)

indicatorNotes.Fixed: letters that are fixed have been rearranged or doctored

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A viewer's gaze fixed on the strong physique of a nude by Titian, the Venetian painter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Powerful body' belongs to the painted nude in the surface; in the answer the body is an international organisation.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: an organisation of member states, whose Security Council can impose sanctions.

entries.clue: Joining old mate among foremost of noisome crossworders? (5)

indicatorNotes.among: the old mate goes among the other letters, inside them
indicatorNotes.foremost of: the foremost letter is the first one

blocks.note: the first letter of Noisome
an ex is a former partner
us, the setter and solvers of crosswords; the question mark flags the liberty

annotation.surface: A former partner joining a smelly bunch of puzzle-solvers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crossworders' are us, the setter and solvers together. 'Joining' reads as a verb in the surface, but it is a noun, a join or connection.
annotation.definitionFit: A nexus is a connection or link between things.
annotation.definitionNote: 'Joining' is a noun here, a junction.

entries.clue: Given final discharge, military unit opening kebab place? (7)

indicatorNotes.final discharge: the word lets go of its final letter, which is the one we keep

blocks.note: TA = Territorial Army, the British Army's volunteer reserve
the last letter of giveN
a door is an opening

annotation.surface: A soldier discharged from the army opens a kebab shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' sounds military, fitting the unit, but it just points at the last letter. The question mark marks the definition as loose: a tandoor is an oven where kebabs are placed, not a shop.
annotation.definitionFit: A tandoor is a clay oven in which meat, including kebabs, is cooked.

entries.clue: Painless choice to remove caps in sanctuary (6)

indicatorNotes.to remove caps: a cap sits on top, which is the first letter in a down entry

blocks.note: EASY, painless, without its first letter
PLUM, a choice thing, without its first letter

annotation.surface: A dentist offering an easy way to have crowns taken off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caps' suggests teeth, fitting 'painless'; here it means the first letters of EASY and PLUM.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in seeking political protection in a foreign country.

entries.clue: Salmon sauce with shortening lacking firmness (7)

indicatorNotes.with shortening: shortening cuts the word, losing its last letter

blocks.note: GRAVY, a sauce, cut short
lax = slack

annotation.surface: A limp salmon sauce made with too much fat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shortening' looks like a cooking fat in a recipe; it tells you to cut the end off GRAVY.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: the Scandinavian dish is raw fish cured with salt, sugar and dill.

entries.clue: Took off from league, leaving fit to get a pint (5)

indicatorNotes.leaving: the fit leaves the word, so its letters come out
indicatorNotes.to get: the gap is filled with what comes next

blocks.note: the starting word
an ague is a shivering fit of fever; it leaves, leaving LE
a + PT, the abbreviation for pint

annotation.surface: A footballer quits the league to go and get fit, then heads off for a pint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like an adjective about fitness; it is a noun, a bout of illness, the AGUE.
annotation.definitionFit: Leapt means sprang, took off from the ground.

entries.clue: Sweet company's manoeuvres to get cuddly (7)

blocks.note: Nestlé's, belonging to the confectionery maker
to nestle is to snuggle in close

annotation.surface: A confectionery firm's corporate manoeuvres to seem friendly.
annotation.walkthrough: The accent is dropped, as usual in crosswords, so Nestlé's company name gives the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Nestlé makes chocolate; someone who nestles settles snugly against another.

entries.clue: Slow lake craft, once (5)

blocks.note: L = lake, on maps
the Argo, the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

annotation.surface: An old boat idling across a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Once' dates the craft to legend: the Argo. Largo is a musical instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction meaning slow and broad.

entries.clue: Watch selection two times on the return (5)

indicatorNotes.on the return: returning, the letters go back the other way

blocks.note: an age and a mo (moment), two stretches of time

annotation.surface: A choice of timepieces shown twice on a return flight.
annotation.walkthrough: AGE + MO reads backwards as OMEGA. The definition is a brand of watch, one choice among many.
annotation.definitionFit: Omega is a Swiss watch brand, one you might select.

entries.clue: Good-for-nothing cryptic clues, no way to break in (9)

indicatorNotes.to break in: NO RD breaks into the jumble of CLUES

blocks.note: anagram fodder
the word itself, added to the fodder
RD = road, a way
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A solver grumbling that cryptic clues are worthless because there is no way into them.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No way to break in' reads as a solver's complaint about hard puzzles; it is really an instruction to add letters to the jumble before rearranging.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a worthless rogue.

entries.clue: Gets wind of change in New York on radio (6)

indicatorNotes.on radio: on the radio it is heard, not seen

blocks.note: cents are small American coins, loose change in New York

annotation.surface: A New Yorker hears on the radio that things are about to change.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Change' is small coins, and New York makes them US cents. 'Gets wind of' works both ways: smelling, and learning of something.
annotation.definitionFit: To scent something is to smell it, or to get wind of it.

entries.clue: Unlimited worms through wharf, reef, or marina (4-4)

indicatorNotes.worms through: the answer wriggles its way through the words, strung across them

blocks.note: wharF REEF OR Marina

annotation.surface: Worms spreading unchecked through a harbour, a reef and a marina.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across three words, ignoring the commas.
annotation.definitionFit: Free-form means not bound by rules or structure, unlimited.
